summary: In September 2018 a new maintainer who had taken over the event-stream npm package added a dependency, flatmap-stream, that contained code targeting the Copay wallet. npm was told on 26 November 2018 and removed the packages.

overview.background: event-stream is a widely used npm package. flatmap-stream 0.1.1 was added as a dependency in event-stream 3.3.6.
overview.impact: Malicious code was deployed in Copay 5.0.2 to 5.1.0 and could harvest keys for accounts holding more than 100 Bitcoin or 1000 Bitcoin Cash.
overview.severity: A targeted supply chain attack with a very broad delivery route.
overview.gaps: npm's post does not say how the malware was first identified.

diagrams.title: A trusted maintainer, an added dependency, a targeted payload
diagrams.caption: Per npm, the attacker posed as a maintainer and took over, then added flatmap-stream, whose code altered the Copay release build.

nodes.label: Attacker takes over maintainership by social engineering

timeline.e: flatmap-stream is added as a direct dependency in event-stream 3.3.6.
Copay builds 5.0.2 to 5.1.0 include the malicious code.
npm's security team is notified of a malicious package in event-stream.
npm removes flatmap-stream and event-stream 3.3.6 and takes ownership of event-stream.
npm publishes its incident analysis and advises users to run npm audit.

rootCause.trigger: Social engineering gave the attacker maintainership of event-stream.
rootCause.underlying: The attacker added a dependency whose code was designed to run only in a specific build environment.
contributing: Handover of an unmaintained popular package
Payload decrypted only in the target environment
Wide use of the package spread the exposure

evidence.label: The takeover
evidence.body: posing as a maintainer, took over maintainership of the event-stream module
evidence.note: From npm's incident analysis as read.

evidence.label: The targeted design
evidence.body: running the payload in any other environment has no effect

diagnose.step: Check the dependency tree for flatmap-stream.
Check which products used the version.

correct.step: Rotate keys if a build ran it.

fix.safety: Do not rebuild signed releases without a clean environment and key rotation.

troubleshoot.scenario: An advisory says a package you depend on includes a malicious dependency that targets your product.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
troubleshoot.answer: Search lockfiles and builds, rebuild clean, rotate release keys and secrets, and tell users what versions are affected.

rootcause.q: Which version of event-stream added flatmap-stream?

design.prompt: Design supply-chain checks for a wallet app.
design.answer: Lockfiles, review, isolated reproducible builds and signing in a clean environment.

options: Removed the packages and took ownership of event-stream
